title: Garden allocator: regionized KV allocation + compact-snapshot compactor
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: KV cache fragmentation is increasing on long-lived GPU hosts under continuous batching workloads. This causes reduced effective cache capacity, increased evictions, and higher tail latency during peak traffic. Goal: introduce a regionized allocation scheme ("Garden allocator") combined with a compact-snapshot background compactor that reclaims fragmented slots without incurring synchronous pauses or heavy synchronous copies. The approach is designed to be compatible with continuous batching windows and KV prefix caching patterns.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end proof-of-concept running on a canary pool with zero client-visible stalls
Measured reduction in fragmentation ratio (free islands / total memory) by >= 40% vs today on 7-day production trace replay
Tail latency (p95/p99) on cold-start-heavy workloads does not regress more than 5%
Memory reclaimed per minute metric and compaction cost telemetry emitting to console dashboards
Safety: compactor can be gated by rollout toggle and fallback to current allocator without state loss
plan: Design: finalize region layout and per-region allocation policy, define snapshot format for live compaction (3 days)
PoC: implement Garden allocator skeleton + tracing hooks; single-host simulation with synthetic fragmentation generator (5 days)
Integration: wire compactor to continuous-batching scheduler, add KV object-level liveness hints and eviction hint API (7 days)
Canary: deploy to warm canary fleet, run 7-day replay with production traces and measure fragmentation, latency, and GPU utilization (10 days)
Rollout: staged rollout with metrics gating and automatic rollback on regressions (3 days)
technical_summary: Garden allocator splits GPU KV memory into small 'beds' (regions) sized according to token residency distribution. Each bed maintains a lightweight free-list and a compactness score. Allocations prefer contiguous runs inside a bed; when contiguous space is unavailable, the allocator places the entry into a tombstoned slot and records a relocation candidate. The compact-snapshot compactor takes periodic, incremental snapshots of target beds and performs copy-on-write relocation in micro-batches aligned to the continuous-batching windows so that compaction work rides in existing GPU work queues rather than adding separate host->device stalls. Snapshots are maintained as short-lived overlays; once relocation completes, pointers are atomically swapped and old pages are freed. This enables pause-free defragmentation and predictable compaction throughput.
experiments: Compare bed sizes (4MB, 16MB, 64MB) to find knee for typical token residency; measure fragmentation ratio and compaction overhead
Measure compaction momentum: run compactor at low, medium, and high aggressiveness and chart reclaimed memory vs CPU/GPU overhead
Replay 7-day production trace with hot-started and cold-start suites to quantify tail-latency and eviction variance
A/B: Canary fleet with Garden vs current allocator; collect per-token hit rates and effective cache capacity
rollout_plan: Feature gated via runtime flag per-cluster
Start with 5% of canary fleet; run 48h smoke tests
Expand to 25% for 7-day trace replay; evaluate metrics
If metrics OK, staged roll to 50% then 100% for non-critical pools; hold enterprise pools behind explicit opt-in
Provide emergency kill-switch that disables compactor and rebinds live pointers back to stable allocator view
risks: Relocation ordering bug can lead to stale pointer reads—mitigate with sequence-numbered swaps and assert checks
Compactor may compete with inference kernel for GPU bandwidth under degenerate load—mitigate by integrated scheduler to throttle compaction during peak SLO windows
Snapshot overlay growth may temporarily increase memory pressure; we cap snapshot concurrency and backoff aggressively
Telemetry gaps could hide regressions—ensure critical metrics are high-cardinality and exported to alerting
